title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Dynamic Handler Exception Close Policy Architecture
purpose: Define exception-aware close policy selection for unexpected accepted WebSocket handler exceptions.
design_summary: `Http3ServerOptions.WebSocketHandlerExceptionClosePolicySelector` lets server owners map the unexpected exception observed from an accepted RFC 9220 WebSocket tunnel handler to a WebSocket close policy. `Http3Server` invokes the selector inside the existing handler-exception catch path, validates selected close payloads with the shared close-frame formatter, and falls back to the configured static handler-exception policy when the selector is absent, returns no policy, throws, or returns an invalid close payload.
data_and_state_considerations: The selector is request-stream scoped when invoked and receives the actual handler exception. The selected policy is not cached across requests, and the fallback static policy remains server-owned configuration.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The existing static 1011/internal-error default remains the final fallback.
Invalid selector output or selector failure emits diagnostics and uses the static fallback policy.
The selector does not replace handlers that explicitly close their own tunnels.
risks: Application selectors can expose exception classification through close codes or reasons, so applications should avoid leaking sensitive details.
External peer behavior still needs live interoperability proof before promoting beyond local loopback evidence.
